first_impression.reaction: Good. It gives me an answer in the first paragraph and doesn't make me scroll through fluff to find it: "A wedding morning timeline is built backwards from the ceremony: fix the time you leave, then the time you must be dressed, then when the photographer arrives, and start the first hair and makeup chair early enough to finish everyone before that." That's a method, not a sales pitch. I skipped to the FAQ first like I always do, then went back to the sample timelines and checked the numbers.

journey.quote: For a 4pm ceremony, for example, that can mean hair and makeup from 9am with a first look or from 10am without one.
journey.reaction: Fine, but for how many people? Without the headcount behind the example I can't tell if 9am is right for us or way off.

journey.section: How long bridal hair and makeup takes
journey.quote: There is no single honest figure to plan around.
journey.reaction: Credit where it's due. Most sites throw out a number they can't back up. Admitting it depends is more believable than a made-up average.

journey.section: Why your trial sets the pace
journey.quote: Get their figures in writing and build the morning on them.
journey.reaction: That's how I'd do it. Get it in writing from the people actually doing the work. Good practical advice.

journey.section: Who goes first and who goes last
journey.quote: Ask your stylist and artist which order suits them.
journey.reaction: It's honest that the order isn't fixed and the people doing the work get the final say, rather than the article pretending there's only one right answer.

journey.section: How the morning moves for earlier and later ceremonies
journey.quote: A 5pm ceremony. Hair and makeup from 11am, first look at 3pm, guests arriving at 4.30pm.
journey.reaction: I checked these against each other. The 2pm and 3pm examples start hair 6.5 hours before the ceremony, the 4pm one starts 7 hours before, and the 5pm one starts 6 hours before. Same first look gap each time, so why does the hair start move around? Probably rounding, but it isn't explained, and when numbers don't line up I start wondering what else is loose.

journey.section: FAQ: How much buffer should you leave on the wedding morning?
journey.quote: In our 4pm examples, 15 minutes sits between the last chair and dressing.
journey.reaction: I went back to check this and couldn't. Neither 4pm sample timeline shows when the last chair finishes, so I can't see that 15 minutes anywhere. Don't point me to a figure in your examples that isn't actually there.

journey.quote: Geoscience Australia's sunrise, sunset and twilight calculator works these times out using the National Gazetteer of Australia.
journey.reaction: A real source with a name I can check myself. More of this, please.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world and is your single point of contact from start to finish, so questions like these go to one person.
journey.reaction: Here's the pitch. "Anywhere in the world" is a big claim with nothing to back it up, and "payments" makes me ask straight away: do you take a cut from the vendors you're paying? The page doesn't say.

journey.section: Plan the morning with one person
journey.quote: If you would like to plan it with someone, a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee agreed in writing before any work starts is the best line on the page for me. It still doesn't tell me how the fee works (flat, percentage, or commissions from suppliers), but at least I'm not going to be surprised by an invoice.

unanswered_questions: How many people in the chairs, and how many stylists and artists, are the 4pm sample timelines based on?
Why does the hair and makeup start time sit a different number of hours before the ceremony in each example (2pm, 3pm, 4pm, 5pm)?
How is the Wedded Advisor fee structured: flat fee, percentage, or something else?
Does Wedded Wonderland or the Advisor take commission or mark-ups from venues and vendors, given they handle payments?
What backs up "anywhere in the world"? Where have you actually planned weddings?

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world and is your single point of contact from start to finish, so questions like these go to one person.
turn_offs_found.why: It's a big claim with no evidence, and mentioning payments without saying whether there's a supplier cut is exactly the hidden catch I'm looking out for.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the sample timelines and the template table

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like to plan it with someone, a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: Fee in writing before any work is a decent signal and the CTA comes after real content, not before it. But I'm comparing three planners and I won't enquire until I know the fee model and whether you take commission from suppliers. This page doesn't answer either, so I'd go hunting on the Concierge page before I'd fill in anything.

top_3_changes: Make the FAQ buffer answer something I can check, since neither sample timeline shows when the last chair finishes. Old: "In our 4pm examples, 15 minutes sits between the last chair and dressing." New: "For example, you might allow 15 minutes between the last chair and dressing."

Make the intro example say what it depends on, so I don't treat 9am as a rule. Old: "For a 4pm ceremony, for example, that can mean hair and makeup from 9am with a first look or from 10am without one." New: "For a 4pm ceremony, for example, that can mean hair and makeup from 9am with a first look or from 10am without one, though your own start depends on how many people are in the chairs."

Tone down the unsupported mid-article pitch, or back it up. Old: "A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world and is your single point of contact from start to finish, so questions like these go to one person." New: "A Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact from start to finish, so questions like these go to one person." (Only if "anywhere in the world" and the payments role can't be supported on the page. The chair should decide.)

open_questions.question: Hair and makeup start sits 6.5h before a 2pm or 3pm ceremony, 7h before 4pm and 6h before 5pm, with the first look 2h before in every case. Is this deliberate (e.g. different assumed headcounts) or should the examples be made consistent? A numbers-minded reader will notice.

Can the page support 'anywhere in the world' and the Advisor handling payments? If yes, a link to the fee and commission explanation would answer this persona's main objection. If not, consider the softer wording in top_3_changes #3.
